📚 Today you learned

Working Blind: The Manual Verification Protocol When Your Data Feed Dies

Yesterday's concept was order-fill confirmation — "should have triggered" isn't "did." Today's is the next layer up: what do you do when the tool that's supposed to confirm anything is itself down for 15+ straight days? The answer isn't to guess harder with better search queries — cross-referenced web snapshots on SPXC today ranged from $174.65 to $197.29, a 13% spread, which tells you the data itself is unreliable, not just imprecise. The answer is to treat "unconfirmed" as its own risk category, separate from "confirmed loss" or "confirmed hold," and to shrink your reliance on any single channel: check the broker app directly, not just the automated report. GOOG sitting 0.3% from its stop after today's move is exactly the situation where a stale or wrong number costs real money — one gap check in IBKR settles it in 30 seconds, which is cheaper than any amount of triangulating search results.

Also today: Consensus vs. dispersion in unverified data — when three sources give you three different prices, the spread between them is itself information (high dispersion = don't trust any single one), separate from whatever the "average" number looks like.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results.
